we developed a new method to measure the lifetime of a femtosecond excited state in nuclear cascade decay, which is a new field of research in the field of nuclear spectroscopy.

the angular correlation of γ-rays emitted in the cascade decay can be measured by a flat crystal spectrometers with a high resolution, which enables to measure the lifetime of a state in the femtosecond region.

the measurement of the lifetime of a low-energy excited state in a nucleus by a precision measurement of a γ-ray spectrum of the state.
a study of the lifetime of nuclear states in the region of 10-12 seconds, which is the shortest among all the nuclear excited states.
the study of the angular distribution of the γ-rays in cascade decays and the lifetime measurements of nuclear excited states.
